page: Amazon Web Services r8in.12xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, providing 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio typical of memory-intensive configurations. The instance contains no onboard GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 75 Gbps, supporting high-throughput inter-node data exchange and distributed cluster architectures. Because the instance lacks local NVMe or solid-state disks, all persistent storage operations rely on external network-attached services such as Amazon Elastic Block Store. Operating on dedicated CPU allocations via the Nitro architecture ensures that processing performance remains consistent without shared-core virtualization contention.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory footprint and 75 Gbps networking capacity position r8in.12xlarge for memory-resident architectures requiring substantial memory density alongside high network throughput. Primary workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data processing frameworks, enterprise in-memory analytics, and extract, transform, load pipelines. The absence of local physical storage requires infrastructure architectures to account for network storage bandwidth, balancing compute density and remote I/O requirements.
